bills.title: To Authorize The Introduction Of A Nonappropriation Bill To Amend The Requirements For A Digital Asset Mining Business And Amend The Authority Of A Local Government With Respect To A Digital Asset Mining Business.

To Authorize The Introduction Of A Nonappropriation Bill To Amend The Requirements For A Digital Asset Mining Business And Amend The Authority Of A Local Government With Respect To A Digital Asset Mining Business.

reading.body:
Arkansas has no AI-specific legislation as of September 2026.

This absence does not mean Arkansas is unaffected by AI development. It means the state has not yet created laws addressing AI systems directly, whether for transparency, liability, labor effects, or data use. Other states and the federal government may impose rules that apply to companies operating in Arkansas regardless.

For AI infrastructure, Arkansas's lack of AI-specific law does not constrain power plants, data centers, or transmission lines. Those follow existing building codes, environmental reviews, and utility regulation. The state's electricity system and available land remain the actual binding factors for whether compute clusters can locate there.

The gap between state AI law and state AI capacity is not unique to Arkansas. Many places hosting significant compute infrastructure have minimal AI regulation on the books.
